findings.topic: TOOLING / coverage note
findings.claim: WebSearch budget for this turn was already exhausted (200/turn shared) before this agent ran; every shop/manufacturer domain tried via WebFetch was EGRESS_BLOCKED (amperepoint.pl, rheidon.com, shelly-api-docs.shelly.cloud, eastroneurope.com, fif.com.pl, orno.pl, ceneo.pl, home-assistant.io, findernet.com, se.com, conrad.pl, docs.evcc.io, pl.farnell.com, pl.rs-online.com, shelly-forum.com). Only GitHub code search was reachable.
findings.detail: Consequence: Allegro PLN prices in this report are unverified estimates (marked low). Shelly API facts, Eastron/ORNO/Finder meter facts and CT apertures were taken from public GitHub fixtures/drivers/docs and are marked per item.

findings.topic: Ampere Point AC500 Smart Load Balancer – connection to WB500
findings.claim: Could NOT be established in this run (all Ampere Point / Rheidon / MediaMarkt sources blocked, no search budget). Interface (RS485 Modbus vs WiFi/proprietary), CT rating, CT cable length, supply and mounting remain unknown.
findings.detail: Two architectures are typical for this class of OEM DLB module: (a) a 'CT box' with 3 split-core CTs that talks to the wallbox over RS485 (2-wire A/B) or a proprietary radio; (b) the wallbox reads a standard RS485 Modbus RTU energy meter (Eastron SDM630 / SDM72D-M V2, Chint DTSU666). Evidence that OEM ecosystems standardise on these meters: Tinkerforge WARP load management uses 'SDM630 oder SDM72 V2' as retrofit phase-current meters; a Chinese inverter/EMS protocol lists meter type options '正泰三相 (DTSU666)' and '东鸿三相 (SDM630)'. Which one AC500 uses must come from its manual (user has it in the AMPERE_POINT folder).

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM / 3EM as DLB meter for wallboxes
findings.claim: Whether Rheidon/Ampere Point firmware accepts Shelly 3EM/Pro 3EM is unknown. Shelly Pro 3EM IS accepted as a grid meter by open energy-management stacks (evcc, OpenEMS, GEMS, Tinkerforge WARP via Modbus TCP), so a wallbox that supports 'Modbus TCP meter' can read a Pro 3EM.
findings.detail: evcc docs ship templates 'shelly-pro-3em', 'shelly-3em-63t-w-gen3', 'eastron-sdm630-modbus', 'orno-or-we-516', 'finder-7m-24', 'finder-7m-38'. Tinkerforge esp32-firmware has a 'Shelly Pro 3EM' register struct inside its meters_modbus_tcp module (Pro 3EM exposes Modbus TCP, port 502, must be enabled in device settings). GEMS manual: 'Shelly 3EM / Pro 3EM / Gen3 3EM-63T: Templates shelly_3em, shelly_pro_3em. Host IP, Port 80'.

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM family – model IDs and variants
findings.claim: Pro 3EM exists in 120 A (default), 400 A and 63 A-CT variants; Pro EM-50 is the single-phase 2-clamp DIN sibling; Gen3 non-DIN siblings are Shelly EM Gen3 (2x50 A) and 3EM-63 Gen3.
findings.detail: aioshelly const.py: MODEL_PRO_EM = 'SPEM-002CEBEU50'; MODEL_PRO_EM3 = 'SPEM-003CEBEU'; MODEL_PRO_EM3_120 = 'SPEM-003CEBEU120'; MODEL_PRO_EM3_3CT63 = 'SPEM-003CEBEU63'; MODEL_PRO_EM3_400 = 'SPEM-003CEBEU400'. ShellyUSA catalog: 'Shelly Pro 3EM – DIN-rail energy meter (3-phase, 120A CT, contactor)'; 'Pro 3EM-400 (3-phase, 400A CT)'; 'Pro 3EM-3CT63 (3-phase, 63A CT, no relay)'; 'Pro EM-50 (1-phase, 2ch, 50A CT, contactor)'; 'Shelly EM Gen3 – Energy meter (1-phase, 2ch, 50A CT)'; 'Shelly 3EM-63 Gen3 – Energy meter (3-phase, 63A CT)'. 'contactor' = built-in relay output (2 A class) intended to drive a contactor coil – usable as an extra trip output in the test board. DIN width of Pro 3EM: 3 modules (~53 mm) – from memory, NOT verified this run.

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM local RPC – EM.GetStatus fields for the HMI
findings.claim: EM.GetStatus (GET http://<ip>/rpc/EM.GetStatus?id=0) returns per phase a/b/c: voltage, current, act_power, aprt_power, pf, freq, errors; plus n_current, total_current, total_act_power, total_aprt_power, errors[].
findings.detail: Field names from real device fixture (Pro 3EM fw 1.1.0): a_current 2.392, a_freq 50.0, a_pf 0.76, ...; n_current: null; total_act_power 558.965. Per-phase error strings: 'out_of_range:active_power', 'out_of_range:apparent_power' (plus voltage/current variants); neutral error 'out_of_range:current'; device errors 'power_meter_failure', 'phase_sequence', 'ct_type_not_set'. EM.GetConfig keys: name, blink_mode_selector, phase_selector ('a'|'b'|'c'|'all'), monitor_phase_sequence (bool), ct_type ('50A'|'120A'|'400A'|'2000A'; Gen3 reports '3x63A'/'3EMG3'), reverse {a,b,c} (flip CT direction in software). Energy totals via EMData.GetStatus / EMData.GetRecords (records have ts, period, count).

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM – neutral current
findings.claim: Standard Pro 3EM (120 A) does NOT measure neutral current: n_current is reported as null on real devices (Pro 3EM and 3EM-63 Gen3 alike). The API reserves the field/neutral errors for hardware that has an N clamp input, but none of the stocked-type Shelly 3-phase meters do.
findings.detail: n_current: null in aioshelly fixture (Pro 3EM 1.1.0) and in matterbridge-shelly mocks for shellypro3em (ct_type 120A) and shelly3em63g3. For N (and PE!) current display use a separate 2-clamp device: Shelly Pro EM-50 (DIN, 2x50 A) or Shelly EM Gen3 (2x50 A) – one clamp on N, one on PE of the output – or an SCT-013-000 100 A/50 mA CT into an ESP32 ADC with burden resistor.

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM – phase sequence detection
findings.claim: Pro 3EM CAN detect wrong phase sequence: set EM.SetConfig {monitor_phase_sequence:true}; status.errors then contains 'phase_sequence'.
findings.detail: OpenEMS driver text: 'PHASE_SEQUENCE_ERROR ... Incorrect phase sequence. Expected A-B-C but found A-C-B.' mapped to error string 'phase_sequence'. Requires all three voltage inputs (L1,L2,L3 + N) wired to the device. Good as a software cross-check of fault F9; keep an independent hardware relay (F&F CKF-B) as the primary feedback.

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM – N-PE voltage / PE monitoring
findings.claim: Pro 3EM has no PE terminal; all voltages are L-N. It cannot see N-PE voltage, open PE, or N-PE swap. Needs an external sensor.
findings.detail: Options for ESP32: (1) ZMPT101B AC voltage-transformer module (isolated, ~5 mA, ESP32 ADC, 0-250 V RMS range, Allegro ~10-25 PLN est.) wired N->PE of the output through a fuse and 2x100 kΩ series resistors – shows N-PE RMS (healthy TN-S: <2 V; broken PEN / F16: tens to 230 V); (2) 230 V AC optocoupler input (e.g. H11AA1 + 2x47 kΩ) as a binary 'PE live > ~60 V' flag; (3) F&F CP-721 single-phase voltage relay between N and PE set to U> ~50 V as a hardware flag. Open-PE detection: inject the 220 kΩ/1 mA path (F3) and measure PE-to-remote-earth with the same ZMPT101B.

findings.topic: Shelly Pro 3EM – update rate on local network
findings.claim: Pro 3EM pushes NotifyStatus over its WebSocket when EM values change (≈ once per second for power values); Home Assistant polls only secondary RPC sensors every 60 s. For the HMI, poll /rpc/EM.GetStatus at 1 Hz over HTTP or subscribe over ws://<ip>/rpc.
findings.detail: HA core const.py: 'RPC_SENSORS_POLLING_INTERVAL: Final = 60' (refresh for polled sensors), 'UPDATE_PERIOD_MULTIPLIER = 2.2'. Power/voltage values arrive as push events, not polling. 1 Hz HTTP polling of one device is well within Shelly's RPC capacity (ESP32-based Pro device). Energy records (EMData) are stored per 60 s period.

findings.topic: Split-core CT geometry (generic 100-120 A class)
findings.claim: Typical 100 A split-core CT (YHDC SCT-013-000) has a 13 mm window and 1 m lead; 120 A class (YHDC SCT-016) has a 16 mm window; 80 A (SCT-010) 10 mm; 200 A (SCT-024) 24 mm.
findings.detail: CircuitSetup README: 'SCT-013-000 100A/50mA CT – 13mm opening, 3.5mm plug'; 'SCT-016 120A/40mA CT – 16mm opening'; 'SCT-010 80A/26.6mA – 10mm opening'; 'SCT-024 200A/50mA – 24mm opening'. BOM elsewhere: 'SCT-013-000 ... 13mm bore, 1m cable'. Shelly's own 120 A clamp is of the same class (hole ≈16 mm, body ≈45x35x30 mm, lead ≈0.5-1 m) – Shelly-specific numbers NOT verified this run. A 16 mm window takes a single 6 mm² (OD ≈5 mm) or 16 mm² (OD ≈8 mm) core easily, but NOT a 5x6 mm² YKY cable (OD ≈17 mm) – and clamping the whole cable would read ~0 A anyway (currents cancel), which is itself a nice 'installer error' demo.

findings.topic: Conductor diameters for CT loops
findings.claim: H07V-K 6 mm²: overall Ø ≈ 4.5-5.3 mm (conductor Ø ≈ 3.4 mm); H07V-K 2.5 mm²: Ø ≈ 3.4-4.0 mm; H07V-K 10 mm²: Ø ≈ 5.7-6.5 mm; H07V-K 16 mm²: Ø ≈ 7.2-8.0 mm. YKY 5x6 mm²: Ø ≈ 16-18 mm; YKY 5x10: ≈ 19-21 mm; YKY 5x16: ≈ 22-25 mm.
findings.detail: From standard HD 21.3 / manufacturer tables (memory, not fetched this run). Design consequence: a 16 mm CT window fits any single core up to 16-25 mm². Required straight run per phase: CT body length (30-45 mm) + 20 mm each side => ≥ 80 mm, recommend 100-120 mm straight, parallel conductors spaced ≥ 40 mm centre-to-centre so three clamps sit side by side; add a 4th loop for N.

findings.topic: Eastron SDM630-Modbus V2 (DIN smart meter, RS485)
findings.claim: 3-phase, 100 A direct connection, 4 DIN modules (72 mm), RS485 Modbus RTU (default 9600 8N1, addr 1, input registers 30001+), per-phase V/I/P/PF/Hz, import/export energy; MID variant exists. The de-facto 'universal' wallbox meter.
findings.detail: Aliexpress title quoted in OpenEnergyMonitor archive: 'SDM630 ... Four Module Three Phase 100A Direct Connection Digital Din Rail Power Meter'; evcc template 'eastron-sdm630-modbus' (brand Eastron, description SDM630-Modbus); Tinkerforge WARP uses SDM630 as the retrofit meter that 'misst Phasenströme'. Register map: Voltage [0,2,4], Current [6,8,10], Power [12,14,16], Frequency 70, Import 72, Export 74 (same map as SDM72D-M per Tasmota config). Allegro price estimate: 320-480 PLN non-MID, 400-550 PLN MID (UNVERIFIED).

findings.topic: Eastron SDM72D-M vs SDM72D-M-2 (V2)
findings.claim: SDM72D-M: 3-phase 100 A direct, 4 modules, Modbus; the original V1 reports totals/energy only, the V2 ('SDM72D-M-2') adds per-phase voltage, current, power, PF – buy the V2 if the ESP32 or DLB needs phase currents.
findings.detail: Tasmota changelog: 'Support for Eastron SDM72D-M three phase 100A Modbus energy meter'. Tinkerforge: load management efficiency improved 'wenn ... Stromzähler ... der Phasenströme misst (SDM630 oder SDM72 V2)' – implies V1 has no phase currents. Homey driver: 'The SDM72D-M-2 is very similar to the SDM630 but supports direct connection up to 100A and has a built-in LCD display. The Modbus registers are mostly compatible with the SDM630'. OpenEMS supports 'SDM630, SDM72D-M-2'. Meter code register 0xFC02 = 0x0089 for SDM72D-M. Allegro estimate: V2 220-320 PLN, V1 180-260 PLN (UNVERIFIED).

findings.topic: ORNO OR-WE-516 / OR-WE-517 (Polish-brand DIN meters)
findings.claim: OR-WE-516: 3-phase energy meter, 80 A direct, RS-485 Modbus RTU, MID; default address 1, 9600 bps; width listed by ORNO as 4.5 modules on the current product page (older listing said 3 modules). OR-WE-517: 3-phase 80 A RS-485 Modbus MID, supported by Tasmota ('Orno WE517-Modbus').
findings.detail: ya-modbus driver README: 'ORNO OR-WE-516 – 3-Phase Energy Meter with RS-485, 80A, MID – Modbus RTU'. homy driver comment: '3-phase energy meter with RS-485, 80A, MID, 3 modules, DIN TH-35mm ... Defaults: address=1 baudRate=9600 dataBits=8 parity=odd stopBits=1' (parity in ORNO manual is given as even in other sources – check meter menu). ORNO URL slug: '3-phase-energy-meter-with-rs-485-80a-mid-4-5-modules-din-th-35mm-5902560322415'. Allegro estimates: OR-WE-516 230-330 PLN, OR-WE-517 260-350 PLN (UNVERIFIED). Easy to buy in PL; register map is float32 holding registers, differs from Eastron.

findings.topic: Finder 7M series
findings.claim: Finder 7M.38 = 3-phase 80 A direct, bidirectional, Modbus RTU (RS485), MID; 7M.24 = single-phase 40 A Modbus. Both have evcc templates. Module widths not verified (7M.38 ≈ 4 modules, 7M.24 1 module from memory).
findings.detail: evcc docs templates: finder-7m-24 ('Finder 7M.24', usage grid, 'RS485 via adapter (Modbus RTU)'), finder-7m-38 ('Finder 7M.38'). evcc changelog: 'Add Finder 7M.24 & 7M.38'. Premium price class – Allegro estimate 600-900 PLN for 7M.38.8.400.0212 (UNVERIFIED). Not recommended when price is secondary but availability matters: fewer Allegro sellers than Eastron/ORNO.

findings.topic: Chint DTSU666 (alternative DLB meter)
findings.claim: Chint DTSU666: 3-phase 80 A direct (or 1.5/6 A CT version), RS485 Modbus, 4 DIN modules – the second meter Chinese OEM chargers/inverters typically list next to SDM630; cheap on Allegro.
findings.detail: Protocol dump lists meter options '正泰三相 (DTSU666)' and '东鸿三相 (SDM630)'; GEMS manual: 'Chint DTSU666 / DTSU666-H 3-Phase Meter'. Allegro estimate 150-250 PLN (UNVERIFIED). Only relevant if the AC500/WB500 manual names it.

findings.topic: What 'smart licznik' means in a Polish EV context – plausible interpretations
findings.claim: Five readings are plausible; the switchboard should reserve space/wiring that covers 1-3.
findings.detail: (1) 'Licznik Modbus dla DLB' – RS485 meter the wallbox/DLB polls for building load (Eastron SDM630/SDM72D-M-2, ORNO OR-WE-516/517, Chint DTSU666); needs 4-5 modules + RS485 terminal pair. (2) 'Licznik MID do rozliczeń' – legally approved sub-meter for billing charging sessions (same devices in MID version; ORNO 516/517 are MID, Eastron SDM630 MID, Finder 7M.38 MID). (3) 'Licznik dwukierunkowy' – prosumer import/export meter (PV context); Pro 3EM, SDM630, SDM72D-M-2 all read bidirectionally. (4) 'Licznik OSD z portem HAN/P1' – utility AMI meter customer interface (in PL rarely usable; Dutch/Belgian P1-DSMR style readers do not apply to most Polish OSD meters) – not something to put in a test board. (5) 'Shelly Pro 3EM jako smart meter' – WiFi/Modbus-TCP meter read by HEMS/evcc; fits the HMI role here.

findings.topic: Phase-sequence / voltage monitoring relays on DIN (hardware feedback for F8/F9/F10)
findings.claim: F&F (Pabianice, PL) line is the cheapest and most available on Allegro: CKF-B (1 module, 3x400 V, phase sequence + phase loss + fixed asymmetry ≈55 V, 1 changeover contact ≈8-10 A), CKF-BR (1 module, with N terminal), CKF-317 (1 module, adjustable asymmetry 40-80 V and delay), CP-730 / CP-731 (3-phase under/overvoltage + asymmetry, 3 modules, adjustable thresholds), CP-721 (1-phase U< 150-210 V / U> 230-260 V, 1 module). Alternatives: Schneider RM4TR32 (22.5 mm, 3-phase sequence/loss/under-over, 2 C/O), Finder 70.31 (3-phase monitor, 35 mm), Zamel CKF/CZF family (codes not verified).
findings.detail: Allegro price ESTIMATES (unverified, typical 2024-25): CKF-B 55-85 PLN; CKF-BR 60-90; CKF-317 80-120; CP-721 70-100; CP-730 150-220; CP-731 170-250; Schneider RM4TR32 450-800; Finder 70.31.8.400.2022 250-400. Use: CKF-B on the OUTPUT (after K_SEQa/b and K_L3) – its contact (via optocoupler or a Shelly digital input) tells the ESP32 that the simulated wrong sequence / phase loss is really present; CP-730 on the output confirms F10a/F10b voltages are outside 207-253 V. All specs from memory of F&F catalogue – fif.com.pl was blocked.

findings.topic: Shelly prices (Allegro, estimates)
findings.claim: Unverified Allegro price ranges for planning only: Shelly Pro 3EM 120A 430-550 PLN; Pro 3EM-400 550-700; Pro EM-50 300-380; Shelly EM Gen3 220-280; Shelly 3EM-63 Gen3 450-550; Shelly 120 A spare clamp 60-90.
findings.detail: No live prices could be fetched (allegro.pl blocked, search budget exhausted). Since the company already stocks 'many Shelly', prices matter only for a missing Pro EM-50/EM Gen3 (N/PE current) if not in stock.

findings.topic: Space allocation summary for metering zone (per this lens)
findings.claim: Reserve on the TH35 rail: Shelly Pro 3EM 3 modules + 1 module gap for clamp leads; optional Pro EM-50 2-3 modules; DIN smart meter 4-5 modules (Eastron 4 / ORNO 4.5) + 2 modules of RS485 + supply terminals; CKF-B 1 module; CP-730 3 modules. Off-rail: 'CT bar' 4 x ≥100 mm straight conductors (L1 L2 L3 N) spaced ≥40 mm, 150 x 60 mm area, located right after the input terminals; plus a 5-core cable loop (~150 mm) for the 'clamp around the cable' demo.
findings.detail: Total ≈ 14-17 modules (vs. 7 assumed in 02_dobor_obudowy.md) if both a DIN meter and Pro 3EM + EM-50 are fitted. CT leads (AC500 to external module): route via a M25 gland or a split cable bushing; ≥ 3 m lead length may be needed to reach the external module – unknown until AC500 CT cable length is known.

recommendations: Treat the AC500 interface as the single most important unknown: ask the user to drop the AC500 manual / box photos (CT labels, connector, 'RS485 A/B' or 'WiFi pairing') into materialy/ before Etap 2; design the metering zone so it works for either architecture (RS485 meter OR CT box).

Build a dedicated 'CT bar' between the input terminals and the main switch: four parallel straight runs (L1, L2, L3, N) of H07V-K 6 mm² (OD ≈5 mm) or 10 mm², ≥100 mm straight each, ≥40 mm pitch, labelled with K/L (source/load) arrows. This hosts the AC500 CTs AND the Shelly Pro 3EM clamps (16 mm-class windows), and lets trainers demonstrate CT faults: wrong phase, reversed direction (Pro 3EM 'reverse' config can be shown), clamp on N, clamp around the whole 5-core cable (= 0 A).

Use the stocked Shelly Pro 3EM as the HMI's live meter: ESP32 polls http://<ip>/rpc/EM.GetStatus?id=0 at 1 Hz and shows a/b/c_voltage, a/b/c_current, a/b/c_act_power, a/b/c_pf, a/b/c_freq, total_act_power; enable monitor_phase_sequence and display errors['phase_sequence'] as the F9 confirmation; use its 'contactor' relay as an extra hardware trip for the main contactor coil chain.

Add a 2-clamp Shelly (Pro EM-50 if the stock has one, else Shelly EM Gen3) with clamp 1 on output N and clamp 2 on output PE: it visualises N current (Pro 3EM cannot – n_current is null) and, with the RCD bypassed (F13), the fault current flowing through PE during N-PE swap/bridge (F5/F6/F16).

For N-PE voltage (PEN break, PE live, open PE) add a ZMPT101B isolated AC voltage module between output N and PE feeding an ESP32 ADC (through fuse + series resistors); show it as a numeric 'U N-PE' tile with a 50 V alarm threshold. Shelly cannot provide this value.

Reserve 4-5 modules + 2 terminal modules for a DIN RS485 meter and buy the Eastron SDM630-Modbus V2 (or SDM72D-M-2 if cheaper) as the default 'smart licznik' – it is the meter most wallbox/DLB firmwares and evcc/OpenEMS understand; wire its RS485 A/B to a 3-position selector: ESP32 (MAX485/RS485 transceiver) OR wallbox/DLB terminal pair, never both masters at once. If the user wants a Polish-brand MID sub-meter instead, ORNO OR-WE-516 (80 A, 4.5 modules, Modbus) is the drop-in.

Install F&F CKF-B (1 module) and CP-730 (3 modules) on the OUTPUT side as independent hardware feedback for phase sequence/loss and over/undervoltage; bring their changeover contacts to ESP32 inputs via optocouplers (or to spare Shelly Pro inputs) so the HMI shows 'fault really present' rather than 'relay commanded'.
Correct the enclosure estimate: metering zone grows from ~7 to ~14-17 DIN modules plus a 150 x 60 mm off-rail CT bar; add an M25 gland or split bushing for the AC500 CT leads to the external module.

When the search budget is restored, verify in one pass: Allegro prices (SDM630 V2, SDM72D-M-2, OR-WE-516, CKF-B, CP-730, Pro EM-50), Shelly 120 A clamp window/lead length, Pro 3EM DIN width, and the AC500 datasheet on mediamarkt.pl/amperepoint.pl.
open_questions_for_user: Which Shelly models and how many are in stock (Pro 3EM 120A? Pro EM-50? Shelly EM / EM Gen3? Pro 4PM / Pro 3 / Pro 1PM / Plus Uni)? The metering layout depends on whether a 2-clamp unit exists for N/PE current.

AC500 Smart Load Balancer: how does it talk to the WB500 – RS485 (A/B terminals), WiFi, or other? What are the CT ratings (e.g. 100 A / 120 A), the CT lead length, and the CT window size (please photograph the CT and the label)? Is the AC500 mains-powered (230 V) or powered from the wallbox?

Does the WB500 app/manual list supported external meters (Eastron SDM630 / SDM72D-M / Chint DTSU666 / Shelly 3EM)? This decides whether a 'smart licznik' slot should host an Eastron (RS485) or whether the Pro 3EM alone suffices.

What is meant by 'smart licznik' for this board: (a) RS485 meter read by the wallbox/DLB, (b) MID sub-meter for billing demo, (c) just a display meter read by the ESP32? Should it also be readable by the ESP32 over RS485?
Supply cable to the board: type and cross-section (e.g. YKY 5x10 mm², OD ≈20 mm)? Needed to size the gland and the CT bar conductors (6 vs 10 mm²).
Should the CT bar also carry the DUT output phases (so the AC500 CTs can be deliberately placed on the wrong side – load instead of supply – as a demonstrated installer error)?
gaps: Ampere Point AC500 Smart Load Balancer: no technical data obtained (interface, CT type/rating/lead length, supply, mounting) – all vendor and retailer domains blocked, WebSearch budget exhausted.
Whether Rheidon/Ampere Point WB500 firmware accepts Shelly Pro 3EM or Shelly EM as the DLB meter – unknown.
Shelly Pro 3EM 120 A clamp exact geometry (window diameter, body size, lead length) and Pro 3EM DIN width – not verified (values given from memory, medium/low).
All Allegro PLN prices – not verified; only estimate ranges given.
F&F CKF-B / CP-730 / CP-721, Schneider RM4TR32, Finder 70.31 exact specs (thresholds, contact ratings) – from memory, manufacturer pages blocked.
Finder 7M.38 / 7M.24 module widths and ORNO OR-WE-517 width – not verified.
H07V-K and YKY overall diameters – from standard tables in memory, not fetched.
